This atlas is a history of AI safety research from the 1950s to 2026, told alongside reinforcement learning and agents, neural networks and language models, and the institutions that fund, build and govern AI. Each has a lane on the map below.

For most of that time the first three were separate fields. They met between 2017 and 2022, when a reward model trained on people's comparisons, first tested on Atari games and a simulated robot, became part of the method behind InstructGPT and ChatGPT. Reward hacking, long seen in game-playing agents, and deceptive alignment, until then mostly argued on paper, became things researchers could test on language models.

```{=html}
<noscript>
  <section class="atlas-source-guide" aria-labelledby="atlas-reading-heading">
    <h2 id="atlas-reading-heading">Read the sources</h2>
    <p>The interactive timeline needs JavaScript. These papers and announcements trace two of its routes.</p>
    <h3 id="thread-human-feedback">How did human feedback reach ChatGPT?</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>In 2017, a model learned what to reward from people comparing clips of simulated robots and Atari agents. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03741">Christiano et al. (2017)</a></li>
      <li>In 2019, the method moved to language models. People compared passages generated by GPT-2, and a model learned to reward the kinds of passages they preferred. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08593">Ziegler et al. (2019)</a></li>
      <li>In 2022, OpenAI used human rankings to train GPT-3 to follow instructions, then applied the method to dialogue for ChatGPT. <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">InstructGPT paper</a> · <a href="https://openai.com/index/chatgpt/">ChatGPT announcement</a></li>
    </ul>
    <h3 id="thread-dangerous-capability-evals">How do safety tests shape model releases?</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>In 2023, Anthropic adopted a policy linking evidence about a model's capabilities to the safeguards required to deploy it. <a href="https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropics-responsible-scaling-policy">Responsible Scaling Policy announcement</a></li>
      <li>In 2025, Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 with stricter safeguards while it was still assessing whether the model had crossed the policy's threshold. <a href="https://www.anthropic.com/news/activating-asl3-protections">Claude Opus 4 release safeguards</a></li>
    </ul>
  </section>
</noscript>
```

## About this atlas

The atlas concentrates on alignment and catastrophic-risk research, and most of its institutional coverage is American and British. Anthropic appears in 16 of the 34 safety entries from 2023 onward, including work with other institutions.

I made the atlas with extensive help from Claude Code and Codex. AI agents drafted most of the cards and checked their dates and sources. I directed the selection and edited the result. Each card lists its sources. Where the main evidence is a developer's report on its own model, the card says so.

Research snapshot dated 8 November 2026. Page revised 18 November 2026. Corrections and additions are welcome as [issues on GitHub](https://github.com/sergeisoly/sergeisoly.github.io/issues).
